html:
The Zunbils were a royal dynasty that ruled Zabulistan, the land south of the Hindu Kush around Ghazni and Kandahar in what is now southern Afghanistan, from about 680 to about 870. The map shows their kingdom around 700.

Their name likely comes from Zun, a sun god whose great shrine stood in Zamindawar. Their origin is debated; they may have come from the Hephthalites or the Turks, and they were related to the Turk Shahis of Kapisa to the north.

For almost two centuries the Zunbils blocked the Arab conquests from Sistan. In 698 they trapped and nearly destroyed an army of the Umayyad Caliphate. They paid tribute when they had to and stopped when they could. In the end they fell not to the caliphs but to the Saffarid ruler Ya'qub ibn al-Layth, who conquered Zabulistan around 870. Its town of Ghazni later became the capital of Mahmud of Ghazni.
